violation_type.title: Assistant Caregivers and Substitutes Comply with Minimum Standard Rules (26 TAC §747.207(2))
violation_type.short_title: Assistant Caregivers and Substitutes Comply with Minimum Standard Rules
violation_type.typical_finding: There was assistant caregiver present who did not have her proof of high school graduation, Orientation to the operation, a background check showing she meets the background check requirements, a notarized affidavit, or a filled out pre-affidaivt.

finding_variants.text: There was assistant caregiver present who did not have her proof of high school graduation, Orientation to the operation, a background check showing she meets the background check requirements, a notarized affidavit, or a filled out pre-affidaivt.

The assistant caregiver did not have  documentation the following    24 hours of preservice training,  Required training for care of children under 24 months  Notarized affidavit  Orientation training  Documentation of high school diploma or GED

During investigation, it was determined that primary caregiver allowed a person to be present, supervising, and transporting children without the person having a personnel file or required caregiver training.     This was corrected at inspection given that the person was not specifically present during the investigation inspection.     The operation informed that the person will no longer be present.
Primary caregiver allowed an unqualified substitute caregiver, help care for children.
Primary Caregiver did not plan for emergency situation and left an unqualified caregiver in charge.
The primary caregiver let her granddaughter who is not a substitute caregiver helping her to take care of children in her childcare home while she searched for the missing victim in the neighborhood.
